Q.1) Scheme X was launched on the occasion of World Mental Health Day in 2022 to provide free
tele-mental health services all over the country, particularly to people in remote or under-served
areas. The scheme will help in providing immediate mental healthcare services and facilitate
continuum of care. It will be implemented in two tiers viz; tier 1 which comprises state Tele-
MANAS cells consisting of trained counsellors and mental health specialists and tier 2 which
comprises specialists at District Mental Health Programme (DMHP)/Medical College resources for
physical consultation and/or e-Sanjeevani for audio visual consultation. Which of the following is
nodal implementing agency for the scheme X?

[a] International Institute of Information Technology-Bangalore
[b] Indian Institute of Technology Bengaluru
[c] National Health Systems Resource Centre
[d] Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Science
[e] National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences, Bengaluru

Solution – [e]

Explanation – The scheme is Tele-MANAS. The nodal Agency is National Institute of Mental Health
and Neurosciences, Bengaluru

Q.2) This scheme was launched in ………….. for assured delivery of maternal and newborn health
care services at no cost visiting public health care centres. All pregnant women, newborns and
mothers up to 6 months of delivery are eligible to get the benefits of the scheme. The services
provided under the scheme include – at least 4 ante-natal check-ups, zero dose vaccination, birth
registration certificates etc. It was launched by integrating three schemes of ministry of health and
family welfare viz; PM Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan, LaQshya and ………………
Fill the gaps

[a] 2019, Janani Suraksha Yojana
[b] 2019, Janani Suraksha Yojana
[c] 2018, Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram
[d] 2018, Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram
[e] 2019, Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram

Solution – [e]

Explanation – The scheme is SUMAN – Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan. It was launched by
integrating three schemes of ministry of health and family welfare viz; PM Surakshit Matritva
Abhiyan, LaQshya and Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram

Q.3) Suraj’s family is living in Maharashtra. His family was the beneficiary of Rashtriya Swasthya
Bima Yojana. The scheme was replaced by another scheme launched in 2018 by PM from Ranchi.
Under the newly launched scheme, government of India provides Rs.5 Lakh health insurance to the
beneficiary families. After the launch of new scheme, Suraj’s family was worried about their
benefits under Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana. Is the Suraj’s family eligible under the scheme
launched in 2018? If yes, how much premium Suraj’s family has to pay to get Rs.5 Lakh health
insurance under the scheme?

[a] The family is eligible and the premium of Rs.436 per annum is required
[b] The family is not eligible
[c] The family is eligible without paying any premium
[d] The family is eligible and the premium of Rs.20 per annum is required
[e] The family is eligible and the premium of Rs.456 per annum is required

Solution – [c]

Explanation – The scheme is Ayushman Bharat Yojana. There is no need to pay any premium to
avail the benefits of the scheme.

I.4) Sameer is a carpenter who lives in Bongaigaon, Assam. He belongs to a BPL family and he is the
sole bread earner of his family. One day, while he was going to his work, suddenly his stomach
started aching. To relieve that pain, he had a painkiller. This continued for some weeks. Another
day, while he was having his dinner, his stomach again started aching and this time the pain was
intolerable. His family took him to the hospital where liver the doctor after doing some tests
diagnosed liver cancer. This was a huge setback for the family because they did not have enough
money to provide treatment for Sameer. Sameer being an aware person had enrolled himself
under a scheme launched in 1997. The scheme has three components out of which, one is the
“Health Minister’s Cancer Patient Fund”. Sameer told his family that he would be fine because the
treatment expenses would be taken care of by the government under the scheme.

[a] Rs.10 Lakhs
[b] Rs.5 Lakhs
[c] Rs.15 Lakhs
[d] Rs.12 Lakhs
[e] Rs.8 Lakhs

Q.5) Pilgrim hospital in Gaya district of Bihar is a district hospital which implements scheme X
launched in 2017 to reduce preventable maternal and new-born mortality, morbidity, and
stillbirths by improving the quality of care provided in the labour room. The scheme caters to every
pregnant woman and new born delivering in public health institutions. The pilgrim hospital has
achieved the NQAS certification, defined quality indicators and 85% of all beneficiaries visiting the
hospital are satisfied with the service. How much incentive will Pilgrim hospital get?

[a] Rs.10 Lakhs
[b] Rs.8 Lakhs
[c] Rs.6 Lakhs
[d] Rs.3 Lakhs
[e] Rs.2 Lakhs

Solution – [d]

Explanation – The scheme X is LaQshya. Facilities achieving NQAS certification, defined quality
indicators and 80% satisfied beneficiaries will be provided incentive of Rs.6 lakh, Rs.3 lakh and Rs.2
lakh for medical college hospital, district hospital and FRUs respectively. Hence, Pilgrim hospital
will get Rs.3 Lakhs as incentive.

Q.6) Under Janani Suraksha Yojana, how much cash assistance will a mother get if she belongs to
Pipli village of Bulandshahar district of Uttar Pradesh?

[a] Rs.1000
[b] Rs.1400
[c] Rs.600
[d] Rs.700
[e] Rs.2000

Solution – [b]

Explanation – Following table shows the assistance provided under Janani Suraksha Yojana –

 Category     Rural Area                   Total       Urban Area                  Total
             Mother’s     ASHA’s                   Mother’s     ASHA’s
             package     package                 package     Package
 LPS         1400       600        2000       1000       400        1400
 HPS        700        600        1300       600        400        1000

performing state i.e. UP

Q.7) Which of the following statements is incorrect with respect to Mission Indradhanush and
Intensified Mission Indradhanush?

[a] Mission Indradhanush provides vaccination against 12 vaccine-preventable disease
[b] Intensified Mission Indradhanush 1.0 was launched in 2017 to improve immunisation coverage
in selected districts and cities and ensure full immunisation to more than 90% people by December
2018
[c] Intensified Mission Indradhanush 2.0 was launched in 2019 to focus on those districts which
have immunization coverage of 70% or below
[d] In Intensified Mission Indradhanush 3.0, the districts were classified as high risk, low risk and
medium risk
[e] Intensified Mission Indradhanush 4.0 was launched in 2021 in 416 districts across 33 states/UTs

Solution – [e]

Explanation – Intensified Mission Indradhanush 4.0 was launched in 2022 in 416 districts across 33
states/UTs

Q.8) Which of the following targets is correct with respect to National Health Mission?

[a] The mission targets to reduce MMR to 25/1000 live births
[b] IMR is targeted to be reduced to 1/1000 live births
[c] The mission targets to reduce TFR to 2.1
[d] Annual Malaria Incidence to be <1/1000
[e] The mission targets to end TB by 2030

Solution – [d]

Explanation – Following are targets of National Health Mission –

    •  Reduce MMR to 1/1000 live births
    •  Reduce IMR to 25/1000 live births
    •  Reduce TFR to 2.1
    •  Prevention and reduction of anaemia in women aged 15–49 years
    •  Prevent and reduce mortality & morbidity from communicable, non- communicable;
       injuries and emerging diseases
    •  Reduce household out-of-pocket expenditure on total health care expenditure
    •  Reduce annual incidence and mortality from Tuberculosis by half
    •  Reduce prevalence of Leprosy to <1/10000 population and incidence to zero in all districts
    •  Annual Malaria Incidence to be <1/1000
    •  Less than 1 per cent microfilaria prevalence in all districts
    •  Ending TB by 2025

Q.9) Identify the scheme launched in 2016 for building an enabling environment for breastfeeding
through awareness generation activities. Under the scheme, 1 award per district is awarded to
best facility. For effective implementation of the scheme, it was decided that Rs.4.3 Lakhs per
district will be spent.

[a] MAA
[b] LaQshya
[c] Mission Parivar Vikas
[d] Project Sunrise

Q.12) Scheme Y was launched in …………. to provide assured, comprehensive and quality antenatal
care, free of cost, universally to all pregnant women on the 9th of every month. Under the
scheme, a minimum package of prenatal care/antenatal care services i.e care given during

Q.14) Match the following schemes with their objectives –

(1) Mission Sampark – (a) For digitization of vaccine stocks and monitors the temperature of the
cold chain through a smartphone application

(3) Mission Parivar Vikas – (c) To accelerate access to contraceptives and high-quality family

Q.15) To develop the backbone necessary to support the integrated digital health infrastructure of
the country, National digital health mission was launched by ministry of health and family welfare.
The scheme was launched in 2020 as a pilot project in some UTs of the country. Which of the
following is not one of the UTs where the scheme was launched as a pilot project?

[a] Delhi
[b] Chandigarh
[c] Ladakh
[d] Puducherry
[e] Lakshadweep

Solution – [a]

Explanation – The scheme is being implemented as a pilot project in UTs of Chandigarh, Dadra and
Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar islands, Lakshadweep and
Ladakh

Q.21) Under Health Minister’s Discretionary Grant, a maximum amount of Rs.1,25,000/- is
provided to patients whose annual income does not exceed Rs.1,25,000/-, to defray a part of the
expenditure on hospitalization/treatment in Government Hospitals for life threatening diseases
covered under RAN in cases where free medical facilities are not available. Which of the following
is/are incorrect with respect to the limits of grants under the scheme?


(1) Rs.75,000, if the estimated cost of treatment is up to Rs.1,00,000

Q.22) Henry olonga is a Zimbabwean citizen who wants to pursue his higher education from India
but he is not able to arrange funds to pay fees of higher education universities in India. His friend
Andy Flower suggested him a scheme of the government of India which targets foreign students to
study in Indian Universities. Under the scheme, Olonga can get up to 100% fee waiver. For availing
this scholarship, Olonga has to give an entrance exam. What is the name of the exam?

[a] SAKSHAM
[b] PRAGATII
[c] SAARTHI
[d] SAATHI
[e] PRABHAV

Solution – [b]

Explanation – The scheme is Study in India. The scholarship exam is PRAGATII (Performance Rating
of Applicants through Global Aptitude Test for Indian Institutions)


Q.23) To train young and budding authors, in order to promote reading, writing and book culture
in the country, and project India and Indian writings globally, a scheme was launched in 2021. The
scheme provides mentorship to young writers and encourages them to write by providing
scholarships. The books prepared under the scheme will be published by National Book Trust.

                                                                                                                        pg. 11

[Type here]



Sachin, who is a resident of Delhi, wants to avail the benefits of this scheme, but he is confused if
he is eligible under the scheme or not. This is because the scheme gives benefits to young authors
and since Sachin is not aware of the maximum age up to which the benefits can be taken. Sachin
was born on 10th July 1991, Is he eligible? Also, how much scholarship amount is provided under
the scheme?

[a] Eligible, Rs.50,000
[b] Not Eligible, Rs.50,000
[c] Eligible, Rs.75,000
[d] Not Eligible, Rs.50,000
[e] Eligible, Rs.1,00,000

Solution – [b]

Explanation – The scheme is YUVA (Young Upcoming and Versatile Authors). Sachin is not eligible
because the scheme provides benefits to authors below 30 years of age. Amount of scholarship
under the scheme is Rs.50,000

Q.24) Scheme Y was launched in 2019 by ministry of education. Under the scheme, Institutes
accredited by the National Accreditation and Assessment Council (NAAC) will guide the non-
accredited institutions to improve their quality standards. The scheme is operationalized through a
Hub & Spoke model wherein the Mentor Institution, called the “Hub” is centralized and will have
the responsibility of guiding the Mentee institution through the secondary branches the “Spoke”
i.e. through the services provided to the mentee for self- improvement. Identify Y.

[a] STRIDE
[b] SPARC
[c] Paramarsh
[d] STARS
[e] Institute of Eminence

Solution – [c]

Q.25) Scheme X was launched in 2013 to provide strategic funds to eligible state higher
educational institutions to address the issues related to equity, access and excellence in higher
education. Jammu and Kashmir applied for this scheme for their faculty improvement. The total
project cost is Rs.1 Crore. How much amount J&K has to contribute out of total project cost?

[a] Rs.10 Lakhs
[b] Rs.40 Lakhs
[c] Zero
[d] Rs.25 Lakhs
[e] Rs.15 Lakhs



                                                                                                                        pg. 12

[Type here]



Solution – [c]

Explanation – The scheme is Rashtriya Ucchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA).

Funding
   •   It is a centrally sponsored scheme
       o  Centre: States – 60:40
       o  Centre: Special category states – 90:10
       o 100% funding for UTs
Hence, J&K, being a UT will not contribute anything as part of the project cost.

Q.26) The Ministry of Education is implementing 2 schemes since 2014 to provide financial
assistance for pursuing technical education to girls and specially-abled children respectively. Jyoti
is one of the two girl children in her family. She admitted herself to the second year of the degree
course through lateral entry and came to know about the scheme. She wants to avail the benefits
of the scheme but her friend, Karishma told her that she is not eligible to take the scholarship
benefits of the scheme. What could be the reason for Jyoti’s ineligibility?

[a] The scholarship is not available for lateral entry students
[b] Her family has two girl children
[c] Her family income is Rs.10 Lakhs per annum
[d] The scheme is meant only for SC girl students but Jyoti is from unreserved category
[e] Her family income is Rs.6 Lakhs per annum

Solution – [c]

Explanation – The two schemes are Pragati and Saksham for pursuing technical education to girls
and specially-abled children respectively. To avail the benefit of these schemes, family income
should not exceed Rs.8 lakh. Hence, option [c] is the correct answer.

This scheme was launched in 1995 as National Program of Nutritional Support to primary
